newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina promises aid to strife-torn province.
newsitem.headline: Argentina promises aid to strife-torn province.

text.p: The government of Argentina promised aid on Thursday to its impoverished northern province of Jujuy where protesters have been blocking major roads demanding jobs.

A storm of protest throughout Argentina's depressed hinterland has caused concern among members of the governing Peronist Party as well as the business community and International Monetary Fund that economic progress cannot continue unless acute social problems are addressed.

Interior Minister Carlos Corach told reporters after a cabinet meeting with President Carlos Menem that the federal government had agreed to help Jujuy generate employment, including bailing out about $80 million in provincial bonds.
"We are working with the Economy Ministry and Jujuy's Finance Ministry ... to redeem the Jujuy bonds," Corach said.
Corach said that the Jujuy protestors had agreed to lift their road blocks following meetings presided over by the Roman Catholic Bishop of Jujuy with provincial and federal government officials.

"We have firm hopes that in the next few hours we will be able to say this situation in Jujuy has been solved," said Corach, adding that the federal and provincial authorities would work to find "short-, medium- and long-term solutions" to the economic problems of the people of Jujuy.
The minister said that many of the bonds to be redeemed were in the hands of the poor.

Since taking power in 1989 and applying free-market policies, the Menem government has crushed once rampant hyperinflation, but Argentine unemployment has soared to over 17 percent. In Jujuy province, unemployment in some towns is as high as 37 percent.
